Psalms 37–41 as numbered in Kittel-Kahle BH3 are numbered 32–36, but the number 41 given after this section of the list may give the total number of Psalms in Book 1 of the Psalms. 41 may, however, be intended to be linked more closely with the numbers which follow, namely, 42–64. Psalms 42 thus has no number attached to it, unless it be 41, but this is more likely to represent the total number of Psalms in Book 1, because summaries of the number of Psalms in each Book are found similarly placed later in the manuscript. From folio 4v to 5v the Psalms are not numbered as part of !he Five Books of Psalms but simply within each book. Psalms 72 is numbered 32 and 32 is the number given to represent the total number of Psalms in Book 2 of the Psalms. According to Kittel-Kahle BH3 the number is 31, but the discrepancy may be connected with the omission of the number 52 on folio 4r. In Book 3 of the Psalms, Psalms 73–89 are numbered 1–17, giving the total 17 for the book and this agrees with Kittel-Kahle BH3. In Book 4 of the Psalms Psalms 93 is omitted. Thus the Psalms are numbered 1–16 and the total given for the book is 16 rather than the 17 numbered in Kittel-Kahle BH3. J: Hebrew; predominantly standard Tiberian, uncantillated and probably added later with a different colour of ink from that of the consonantal text.
K: Esther 9:15–22; Examples of non-standard vocalization occur. The original problem in the unvocalized text was a dittograph of the whole of Esther 9:16 by homoioteleuton with ובבזה לא שלחו את ידם in 9:15. Probably the scribe who vocalized the manuscript deleted the dittograph by crossing each word through, but a second and probably inexpert hand has deleted the first half of the copy of 9:16 which remained in the text as corrected by the scribe who vocalized the manuscript, and substituted for it the opening words of 9:17, namely, ביום שלשה עטר לחדש אדר. This is an error by homoioteleuton with ונוח, which occurs in both 9:16 and 9:17. Thus in the text as we have it, the first half of Esther 9:16 is missing. At Esther 9:18 בו, which has been omitted from the text before ובארבעה, is supplied above the line and the dittograph ונוח בחמשה עשר בו is deleted by being crossed through, probably by the scribe who vocalized the manuscript, since the dittograph is not vocalized. ועשה, which had also wrongly been deleted is rewritten, above the line in a different hand and with the same colour of ink as that of the vocalization and deletions.

Examples of non-standard vocalization occur. On folio 1r after Joshua 24:10 the rubric כי המצוה הזאת indicates that the passage ending with Isaiah 49:13 in the second column is the Haphtorah for a Seder beginning at Deuteronomy 30:11. On folio 1v part of Joshua 1:8 is written in the margin between the columns, after Joshua 1:9 there is the rubric בי יאיר[ ]. And before Ezekiel 46:1 the rubric בט וחודט יחזק[ ] indicates that the passage which follows is the Haphtorah for טבת החרט. On folio 2r before 1 Samuel 15:2 the rubric זכר indicates that the passage which follows is the Haphtorah for טבת זכור and before Ezekiel 36:25 the rubric פרה יחזק indicates that the passage which follows is the Haphtorah for טבת פרה. On folio 2v before Malachi 3:10 the rubric תע indicates that the Haphtorah which follows is taken from the Minor Prophets and before Judges 5:1 the rubric טופ indicates that the Haphtorah which follows is taken from Judges. Cf. T-S B17.21 and 24 in Volume 1.
